target.title: Install ClawHub packages for new Claw agents
target.body:
## Summary

- resolve every exact ClawHub package artifact, trust decision, install/reuse action, and plugin runtime id into the consented add plan
- install skills into the new agent workspace and plugins through the existing shared-host plugin lifecycle, enforcing the consented artifact digest at apply time
- persist pending/complete/failed/rolled-back package provenance in the canonical shared-state schema
- run package mutation after workspace/config/file mutation and compensate newly installed shared plugins in reverse order when a later package fails
- warn across CLI, Gateway, and Control UI plugin removal when Claw provenance references the shared plugin, including version drift and uncertain state

## Scope

This is the package-owner slice of the experimental Claw lifecycle. It keeps the grouped RFC contract (`packages[].kind`, `source`, `ref`, and exact `version`) and deliberately does not restore generic artifact selectors or agent skill lists. MCP servers and cron jobs remain blocked for later stack slices.

Dry-run resolves each package to an exact artifact digest and owner action. Apply requires the matching plan digest and rechecks package owner state and artifact identity immediately before mutation. Exact existing packages are reused by adding a Claw reference; conflicting versions, digests, runtime identities, or ownership state fail closed.

Skills are workspace-scoped. Plugins remain process-wide shared-host resources and are not represented as agent-isolated. For this experimental v1, explicit `claws add --yes --plan-integrity <exact-preview-digest>` consent authorizes the displayed shared plugin install/reuse action. Per-agent plugin isolation is out of scope and can be revisited separately.

Package references describe dependency provenance, not exclusive ownership. A reused operator package is independently owned. A Claw-started install is journaled before external mutation. Conclusively compensated plugins become `rolled_back`; uncertain failures remain visible. Plugin uninstall stays operator-controlled and warns for relevant Claw references.

The CLI remains gated by `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`.

## Stack

- RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27
- Depends on: #101973 managed workspace files
- This PR: package owner preflight, installers, provenance, compensation, and shared uninstall warnings
- Next: #102296 status and remove

## Validation

- 75 focused unit tests passed, 1 skipped; 6 lifecycle E2Es; 27 plugin tests; 25 Claws CLI tests; 2 exact skill-artifact regressions
- final SRI follow-up: 7 package tests and 2 exact skill-artifact tests passed
- scoped Oxfmt/Oxlint and `git diff --check` passed
- generated Kysely verification, raw-SQL guardrails, and SQLite transaction-boundary checks passed
- core tsgo has no changed-file error; it reports four existing cross-worktree declaration-path errors
- GitHub CI was clean on the preceding exact head; the final SRI compatibility follow-up is rerunning

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
`claws add` must resolve and consent-bind real ClawHub package bytes, install a declared skill into the new agent workspace, retain truthful partial provenance, and reject downloaded bytes that do not match the consented digest.

Real environment tested:
Windows 11, exact OpenClaw source head `ae79fd7ddd7cc7f1d672bf1b91fa927e7b159e89`, portable Node `v24.15.0`, isolated temporary OpenClaw home/config/state, production `https://clawhub.ai`, public `@steipete/weather@1.0.0`, real CLI/registry/archive/workspace installer/SQLite provenance paths. The partial-state case used the same source runtime and SQLite paths with a deterministic injected package-boundary disconnect after pending provenance was written.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Created an isolated grouped development manifest declaring agent `proof-weather` and skill `@steipete/weather@1.0.0`.
2. Ran `node --import tsx src/entry.ts claws add <manifest> --dry-run --json` with the experimental gate and isolated state environment.
3. Ran `node --import tsx src/entry.ts claws add <manifest> --yes --plan-integrity <preview digest> --json` against production ClawHub.
4. Called the real ClawHub skill installer for the same release with an intentionally wrong SHA-256 SRI pin and checked the workspace for `SKILL.md`.
5. Ran `applyClawAddPlan` in an isolated source harness with a deterministic disconnect injected after real pending package provenance persistence, then read the root install and package-reference rows back from SQLite.

Evidence after fix:
```text
HEAD=ae79fd7ddd7cc7f1d672bf1b91fa927e7b159e89
NODE=v24.15.0
preview.ready=true preview.blockedActions=0
package.target=clawhub:@steipete/weather@1.0.0
package.digest=sha256-R+SuEUGYM818esrCm9Hl5N00ZzMWgQeYKg9zp0i6OMk=
apply.status=complete configCommitted=true agent=proof-weather
package.status=complete ownership=claw-installed
skill.SKILL.md.exists=true installedOwner=steipete installedVersion=1.0.0
artifact.sha256=47e4ae11419833cd7c7acac29bd1e5e4dd346733168107982a0f73a748ba38c9

wrong-pin.result.ok=false
wrong-pin.error=ClawHub archive integrity mismatch: expected sha256-AAAA...AAA=, got sha256-R+Su...OMk=.
wrong-pin.skillWritten=false

injected-failure.result.status=partial
injected-failure.configCommitted=true workspaceCreated=true
injected-failure.rootRecord.status=config_committed
injected-failure.packageRef.status=failed ownership=claw-installed
injected-failure.configAgents=main,proof-weather
```

Observed result after fix:
The exact artifact digest appeared in the preview and consented plan, the real production archive installed successfully into the new agent workspace, and the same digest was recorded in both origin metadata and Claw package provenance. A wrong digest failed before extraction. A later package-boundary failure preserved the committed agent/workspace plus a queryable failed package reference instead of losing ownership evidence.

What was not tested:
No live process-wide plugin was installed or reused in this proof, and no Crabbox host was used. Plugins remain intentionally shared-host resources under exact-plan experimental consent; per-agent plugin isolation is not claimed by this PR.
